example.detection_method: Deploy email gateway filters with machine learning models and YARA rules to detect lookalike domain names and suspicious tokenized URLs. Correlate email sender IPs and DKIM/SPF anomalies with threat intelligence databases. Implement user training campaigns using example phishing templates to improve recognition of subtle domain name typosquatting. Monitor DNS logs for lookalike domain queries. Use UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) to detect unusual access patterns to invoice portals from CFO or finance roles.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1589.002 - Gather Victim Identity Information: Search Open Websites/Domains
T1598.002 - Phishing for Information: Spearphishing via Service
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a spear phishing scenario targeting a high-value individual (CFO) with a highly tailored email containing a malicious link hosted on a lookalike domain. The technical data is comprehensive, including realistic email headers, SMTP transaction logs, domain registration details showing recent creation and privacy protection, URL obfuscation examples, webserver access logs, and DNS query logs. Indicators clearly highlight suspicious domains, IP addresses, email subject and sender, malicious URL patterns, and DNS queries, all supporting the spear phishing nature. The detection method is detailed and aligns well with recommended risk reduction strategies, including email filtering, threat intelligence correlation, user training, and behavioral analytics. Relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques are correctly identified and appropriate for the scenario. Overall, the sample is realistic, complete, and well-aligned with the problem description and risk reduction measures.
